items.statement: The adjacent complete statements, assumptions and formula proofs describe the exact generic results; the optional Lean is initially folded.
assumptions: E has real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional and Borel structures; no positive dimension is required.
The only mathematical data are E with its finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures, and a finite real polynomial p.
The returned operator estimates apply to the same derivative field in the ambient derivative conclusion; both endpoint weights in the difference estimate satisfy norm at most one.
p is any finite real polynomial, including zero, constant and non-even polynomials. The weight w ranges over all of E.

formulae.label: A Gaussian polynomial feature has its actual ambient L² derivative
The same Gaussian derivative is bounded and Lipschitz on the closed unit ball

obligations.label: A Gaussian polynomial feature has its actual ambient L² derivative
The same Gaussian derivative is bounded and Lipschitz on the closed unit ball

bindings.boundary: This is a full ambient derivative, not merely a derivative along the unit sphere or along one fixed direction.; The theorem does not assert continuity of the derivative field, a second Fréchet derivative, a risk-potential identity or a manifold gradient.

assumption_deltas.source: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let γ be its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and let p be any finite real polynomial. For every ambient w and every direction v, both f_w(x)=p(⟨w,x⟩) and d_{w,v}(x)=p′(⟨w,x⟩)⟨v,x⟩ belong to L²(γ). There exist simultaneous membership witnesses and a field D(w):E→L²(γ) of continuous real linear maps such that D(w)v is exactly the class of d_{w,v}. The actual feature-class map Φ(w)=[f_w] is fully Fréchet differentiable at every ambient w, with derivative D(w). No feature membership, derivative membership, domination, differentiability or operator bound is an input.

assumption_deltas.source: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let γ be its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and let p be any finite real polynomial. For every ambient weight w and direction v, the actual functions f_w(x)=p(⟨w,x⟩) and d_{w,v}(x)=p′(⟨w,x⟩)⟨v,x⟩ belong to L²(γ). There exist simultaneous membership witnesses and a field of continuous real linear maps D(w):E→L²(γ), with D(w)v=[d_{w,v}], such that the actual feature-class map Φ(w)=[f_w] is fully Fréchet differentiable with derivative D(w) at every ambient w. There also exist strictly positive real constants M₁,M₂ such that ‖D(w)‖op≤M₁ for every ‖w‖≤1 and ‖D(u)−D(w)‖op≤M₂‖u−w‖ whenever both weights lie in the closed unit ball. The constants may depend on p and the ambient space; no dimension-independent rate is asserted. All memberships, derivatives and bounds are produced.

items.statement: The adjacent complete statements, assumptions and formula proofs describe the exact generic results; the optional Lean is initially folded.
assumptions: E,H are complete real inner-product normed spaces. F and D have the explicit actual full ambient Fréchet derivative relation.
M₁,M₂ are nonnegative; uniform derivative and operator Lipschitz bounds are explicit inputs on the closed unit ball. The tangent and joint field bounds require unit endpoint weights.

formulae.label: A Hilbert feature potential has a controlled tangent Riesz field

obligations.label: A Hilbert feature potential has a controlled tangent Riesz field

bindings.boundary: D, its actual derivative identity and the two operator bounds are explicit generic hypotheses; a concrete feature model must produce them separately.; The conclusion is a tangent Riesz representation. Equality with a chosen manifold-gradient API, a geodesic-distance or law-Wasserstein estimate, and a uniform residual bound are separate obligations.

assumption_deltas.source: Let E,H be complete real inner-product normed spaces. Let F:E→H be a map, and let each D(w):E→H be a continuous real linear map satisfying the actual ambient identity DF(w)=D(w) for every w. Suppose M₁,M₂≥0, ‖D(w)‖op≤M₁ on the closed unit ball, and ‖D(w)−D(u)‖op≤M₂‖w−u‖ there. For r∈H define V_r(w)=2⟨r,F(w)⟩ and G_r(w)=2(D(w)*r−⟨D(w)*r,w⟩w), where * is the Hilbert adjoint. At every ambient w, V_r has derivative 2⟨D(w)*r,·⟩. At every unit w, G_r(w) is tangent, satisfies ⟨G_r(w),v⟩=2⟨r,D(w)v⟩ for every v perpendicular to w, and has norm at most 2M₁‖r‖. For all r,q and unit w,u, its joint increment is bounded by 2M₁‖r−q‖+2(M₂+2M₁)‖q‖‖w−u‖.

items.statement: The adjacent complete statements, assumptions and formula proofs describe the exact generic results; the optional Lean is initially folded.
assumptions: K is strongly measurable and bounded by the nonnegative B. c is jointly measurable, nonnegative and bounded by nonnegative C.
L≥0 and the displayed feature increment bound holds for every pair; symmetry, a triangle inequality and an optimal coupling are not assumptions.
U is measurable; H is a complete real normed vector space. μ and ν are actual probability measures.

formulae.label: Actual Bochner means are controlled by the all-coupling quadratic cost

obligations.label: Actual Bochner means are controlled by the all-coupling quadratic cost

bindings.boundary: The all-coupling infimum is literal extended nonnegative transportCost; real conversion occurs after finite cost is proved. No optimal coupling or attainment is assumed.; This is a generic bounded-cost theorem. A round-geodesic metric identification, a concrete Gaussian feature Lipschitz estimate, and their particular Wasserstein instance must be established separately.

assumption_deltas.source: Let U be any measurable space and H a complete real normed vector space. Let K:U→H be strongly measurable with ‖K(u)‖≤B. Let c:U×U→ℝ be measurable with 0≤c(z)≤C, and suppose ‖K(u)−K(v)‖≤L c(u,v), where B,C,L≥0. For any two probability measures μ,ν on U, define Q as the infimum, over all actual couplings π with these two marginals, of ∫c² dπ, interpreted as an extended nonnegative integral; set W=Q^(1/2). Then K is genuinely Bochner integrable under each law, Q is finite, and ‖∫K dμ−∫K dν‖≤L W.toReal. For every y∈H both residual norms are at most B+‖y‖. No optimizer, chosen-plan bound, finite-cost assumption or mean-identity premise is supplied. U need not carry a vector-space structure, and c need not be a metric.
